alternatives_considered.approach: Store a per-membership balance column updated on every expense/payment write
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Violates the project invariant that balances are derived by one recompute path and never stored; a stored column can drift from the ledger and needs its own locking, while recompute in-request is already budgeted for groups up to 200 members (TR-9 non-functional note)

alternatives_considered.approach: Exact-minimum settlement search instead of greedy min-cash-flow
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Minimum-transfer settlement is NP-complete (subset-sum); ADR-0005 already decided greedy min-cash-flow with the at-most-N-1 guarantee, and the issue contract names that algorithm explicitly

alternatives_considered.approach: Restrict settle-up endpoints to current members only and leave departed seats unsettleable
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A leave-at-zero followed by an expense edit or delete touching the departed seat strands a non-zero net no payment could ever clear, breaking the issue's own promise that the group reads all-zero; letting a current member record with a departed ledger participant of the same group keeps every net settleable without touching expense code

issue_snapshot.title: Balances with simplified debts and settle-up payments
issue_snapshot.body:
Members can see who owes whom with at most N-1 simplified transfers and record settle-up payments until the group reads all-zero.

Person sees: group debts card with Settle-up buttons, balance banner (settled or owes-summary), home totals cards (you-are-owed, you-owe), per-person rows and group list with per-group balances. Contract: CONSUMES the expense and payment ledger; DEFINES lib/settle net balances plus greedy min-cash-flow simplification and Payment writes and deletes as ledger entries, never balance edits. Constraints: TR-9 with at most N-1 transfers, balances derived by one recompute path and never stored, involved-member-only payment delete.

**Risk.** Money-trust risk: balances derived by one recompute path and never stored, greedy min-cash-flow capped at N-1 transfers, payments as ledger entries with involved-member-only delete.

**Out of scope**
- Activity feed UI
- Seed data and deploy guide
- Moving money in the app (settle-up only records payments, per spec)

Covers: TR-3, TR-9, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #6.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Group page shows per-member net balances plus simplified who-pays-whom with at most N-1 transfers via the stated greedy min-cash-flow, with an explicit settled and all-zero state
- **IAC-2** Home shows cross-group you-owe and you-are-owed totals per person alongside per-group balances
- **IAC-3** Record full and partial settle-up payments from the debts card with a confirm, delete them as an involved member with a confirm, and see balances update in place with an aria-live announcement
- **IAC-4** Amounts render in the group currency from one formatter with tabular numerals; the debts card sits above expenses on narrow screens

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

review.title: A payment between two departed seats can be recorded but never deleted, stranding a mistaken write with no recourse.
review.detail:
A payment between two departed seats can be recorded but never deleted, stranding a mistaken write with no recourse.

`lib/settle/actions.ts:173`

Evidence: createPayment accepts any two ids present in the computeNetBalances map (actions.ts:102-107), and that map includes departed ledger participants (balances.ts departed fold); simplifyDebts explicitly allows transfers naming departed holders and SettleUpForm offers every suggested transfer for recording. deletePayment then requires the acting current member to be the payer or the recipient (actions.ts:173-177) — but neither endpoint is a current member, a departed seat holds no session, and there is no owner override — so the delete is refused forever and the nets stay wrong.

Fix: Require at least one endpoint to be a current membership when creating a payment, or allow any current member to delete a payment whose endpoints are both departed.

review.title: The work order's promised transaction-atomicity case for settle writes was not written: no test fails a payment write mid-transaction.
review.detail:
The work order's promised transaction-atomicity case for settle writes was not written: no test fails a payment write mid-transaction.

`lib/settle/actions.test.ts`

Evidence: work-order.json tests for lib/settle/actions.test.ts list 'failing write leaves no payment and no activity row (transaction atomicity)'; the 711-line file (18 cases) proves refusals write nothing and proves create/delete round-trips, but grep for atomic/rollback/half-written/part-way finds nothing, while lib/expenses/actions.test.ts:692 proves the identical single-tx shape with a mid-write mock failure ('leaves nothing behind when the write fails part-way through'). The tx closure itself follows the proven pattern, so this is coverage debt, not a suspected half-write.

Fix: Add a mid-transaction failure test mirroring the expense one (throw between the payment insert and the activity insert, assert no payment and no activity rows remain).

triage.diagnosis: root-cause did its work and the harness threw it away. This run's session wrote a complete work order — the transcript records `Write /home/runner/work/tabs-v3/tabs-v3/work-order.json (10905 chars)` — and the diagnose job's next-to-last step then overwrote that file with the session's StructuredOutput object, which is a hand-typed condensation: 3643 chars, acceptance[] holding only AC-1..AC-4 and AC-9, each with `id` and `check` and no `source` at all. post-work-order.mjs:82 therefore refused it as neither answering nor deferring IAC-1..IAC-4, which is correct on the document it was given — and it refuses before the root-cause-specific "dropped AC-x" check on line 93 is ever reached. framework_defect.what: The diagnose job's step "The result of \"Diagnose\", as its file" (lines 451-468) replaces work-order.json with the session's StructuredOutput — its comment says so deliberately — and no gate is applied to that result before the artifact is handed on. The split-criteria check first sees it in the publish job's post-work-order.mjs:82, after the session has ended and in another job, so the session can never be told which fields its result lost. Meanwhile claude-args.mjs appends to the prompt: "Before you finish, run: node .sdlc/bin/preflight.mjs --issue N. It runs, on the files you wrote, exactly the checks this job applies to them after you finish: the schema, the report's own consistency, the evidence, reserved paths and the split's criteria" — false for a gated artifact, because the file preflight reads is thrown away and the checks run on the structured result instead. The stage is therefore a loop with no exit: the agent writes a clean file, preflights it clean, returns a schema-valid condensation of it, and the run dies on the condensation. The identical step is in sdlc-plan, sdlc-implement, sdlc-qa, sdlc-review and sdlc-main-verify, so any gated artifact can be lost this way; issue #7 has now paid for it twice.
framework_defect.fix: In that step, after writing the file from the result, run the gates the publish job runs on the file just written — `node .sdlc/bin/sdlc-ctl.mjs validate --schema work-order --file work-order.json`, `check-forbidden.mjs --file work-order.json`, `check-split-criteria.mjs` (the same list as GATES['work-order'].then in lib/gate-checks.js, which preflight already uses). When one refuses, do not hand the artifact over: start one more session with the refusal text as its prompt — the pattern "Finish — Diagnose" already uses for a session that ended without its result — so the session is told which fields its result dropped and can return the whole work order; hand over only a file that passes its own gates. That is the same move check-split-criteria.mjs's own header describes for the planner: run the check where the producer can still act on it, not in a job after it. The resolving defect in the prompt (claude-args.mjs — a rule, so a person's call either way) is that it must say the JSON returned through StructuredOutput is what becomes the artifact and what the checks run on, not the file the agent writes.
